title: SemanticNVS: Improving Semantic Scene Understanding in Generative Novel View Synthesis
claim: Conditioning a multi-view diffusion model on warped and iteratively completed pretrained semantic features improves scene understanding and generation quality.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, central timestep box with feedback loop arrow on top
description: A left-to-right pipeline diagram. The left panel shows the inputs: an input image, its DINO feature map and a camera trajectory sketch. The large central panel, labeled Timestep t, is split by a dashed line into an input view row and novel view rows. Warped DINO features are merged into completed features, which sit beside warped RGB, ray maps and noisy latents joined by circled-plus symbols. These feed a blue hourglass-shaped Multi-View Diffusion block. On the right of the block are one-step denoised images, and a DINO trapezoid extracts features from them. A black arrow loops back over the top, labeled 'Combine with M_R', to the merged features. The right panel shows the output input and novel images. Yellow highlight boxes mark the DINO feature maps, which draw the eye first.
caption: Method Overview. SemanticNVS integrates semantic DINO features into the multi-view diffusion setup in two different ways. First, it provides warped features from the given input view and uses them as additional conditioning. Second, it extracts DINO features from intermediate generations ˆxt
abstract: We present SemanticNVS, a camera-conditioned multi-view diffusion model for novel view synthesis (NVS), which improves generation quality and consistency by integrating pre-trained semantic feature extractors. Existing NVS methods perform well for views near the input view, however, they tend to generate semantically implausible and distorted images under long-range camera motion, revealing severe degradation. We speculate that this degradation is due to current models failing to fully understand their conditioning or intermediate generated scene content. Here, we propose to integrate pre-trained semantic feature extractors to incorporate stronger scene semantics as conditioning to achieve high-quality generation even at distant viewpoints. We investigate two different strategies, (1) warped semantic features and (2) an alternating scheme of understanding and generation at each denoising step. Experimental results on multiple datasets demonstrate the clear qualitative and quantitative (4.69%-15.26% in FID) improvement over state-of-the-art alternatives.
